text:

query: within-run and across-run adaptation agent training
text:
1. **[A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.21046)** (2026). Closest conceptual match: explicitly distinguishes **intra-test-time** and **inter-test-time** adaptation across models, memory, tools, and agent architectures. **People:** Huan-ang Gao (Tsinghua), Jiayi Geng (Princeton), Wenyue Hua (UC Santa Barbara), and collaborators; corresponding authors Hongru Wang (University of Edinburgh) and Mengdi Wang (Princeton).

2. **[Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.11366)** (2023). Agents reflect on feedback and retain textual memories to improve subsequent attempts, without updating model weights. **People:** Noah Shinn, Federico Cassano, Edward Berman (Northeastern); Ashwin Gopinath (MIT); Karthik Narasimhan and Shunyu Yao (Princeton).

3. **[RL²: Fast Reinforcement Learning via Slow Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1611.02779)** (2016). Foundational training approach connecting rapid adaptation during a trial with slower learning across training trials; recurrent memory persists across episodes within each trial. **People:** Yan Duan, John Schulman, Xi Chen, Pieter Abbeel (UC Berkeley and OpenAI); Peter L. Bartlett (UC Berkeley); Ilya Sutskever (OpenAI). Affiliations are those listed in the paper.

4. **[Stanford CS329A: Self-Improving AI Agents](https://cs329a.stanford.edu/)** (Autumn 2025). Useful course and reading list covering test-time improvement, learning from feedback, memory, reinforcement-learning training, and agent evolution. **People:** instructors Aakanksha Chowdhery and Azalia Mirhoseini (Stanford University).

query: LLM agent training environment evolves with policy
text:
1. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16523v1)** — Closest match: a meta-agent modifies the environment, user simulator, rewards, and training configuration while the policy learns, applying validated changes during ongoing training.

2. **[SEAL: Synergistic Co-Evolution of Agents and Learning Environments](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.24426v1)** — Uses agent failures to jointly improve the policy and the environment’s tool descriptions, constraint information, and recovery feedback.

3. **[CoEvolve: Training LLM Agents via Agent-Data Mutual Evolution](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.15840v1)** — A closely related approach: training tasks evolve with the agent’s weaknesses, using rollout feedback to synthesize and validate new tasks within environments.  
   **People:** Shidong Yang, Ziyu Ma, Tongwen Huang, Yiming Hu, Yong Wang, and Xiangxiang Chu—all affiliated with AMAP, Alibaba Group.

query: multi-turn reinforcement learning user simulation benchmarks
text:
1. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.19736v1)** — A close match: standardized environments pairing agents with simulated users for multi-turn RL training and evaluation. **People:** Cheng Qian (Salesforce AI Research and UIUC), Heng Ji (UIUC), Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, and colleagues (Salesforce AI Research).

2. **[LMRL Gym: Benchmarks for Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning with Language Models](https://lmrl-gym.github.io/)** — Eight tasks spanning dialogue and text games, with online simulators and offline training datasets; tests information gathering, strategy, and credit assignment. **People:** Marwa Abdulhai, Isadora White, Charlie Snell, Charles Sun, Joey Hong, Yuexiang Zhai (UC Berkeley); Kelvin Xu (Google DeepMind); Sergey Levine (both).

3. **[ColBench / SWEET-RL: Training Multi-Turn LLM Agents on Collaborative Reasoning Tasks](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.15478v1)** — Collaborative programming and frontend-design benchmark paired with an RL method that provides turn-level learning signals. **People:** Yifei Zhou (FAIR at Meta and UC Berkeley), Sergey Levine (UC Berkeley), Song Jiang, Yuandong Tian, Jason Weston, Sainbayar Sukhbaatar, and Xian Li (FAIR at Meta).

4. **[τ²-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.07982v1)** — Tests multi-turn coordination with simulated users who can also operate tools and change the shared environment. Particularly relevant for evaluating agents trained through user interaction. **People:** Victor Barres, Soham Ray, Karthik Narasimhan (Sierra); Honghua Dong (Sierra, University of Toronto, Vector Institute); Xujie Si (University of Toronto and Vector Institute).

query: editable training systems for tool-using agents
text:

2. **[Symbolic Learning Enables Self-Evolving Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.18532v1)** (2024). Treats prompts, tools, and agent workflows as editable, learnable components, optimized using language-based feedback. **People:** Wangchunshu Zhou, Yixin Ou, Shengwei Ding, Yuchen Eleanor Jiang, and collaborators; the original paper lists **AIWaves Inc.**

3. **[ToolBrain: A Flexible Reinforcement Learning Framework for Agentic Tools](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.00023v1)** (2025). Customizable tool-use training with programmable rewards, task generation, and distillation. **People:** Quy Minh Le and Minh Sao Khue Luu (ToolBrain Research); Khanh-Tung Tran, Duc-Hai Nguyen, and Hoang D. Nguyen (University College Cork); Quan Le (CeADAR, University College Dublin); Hoang Thanh Lam (IBM Research Dublin); Hoang-Quoc-Viet Pham (ToolBrain Research).

4. **[AgentTune: A Unified Training Lifecycle for Tool-Using LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.13335v1)** (2026). Composable training and evaluation infrastructure, including YAML-defined workflows and corrective retraining. **People:** R E Zera Marveen Lyngkhoi, Abhivansh Gupta, Vidushee Vats, Ram Mohan Rao Kadiyala, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu, and Pratinav Seth — **Lexsi Labs**.

query: methods improving user-centric agents with simulated users
text:
1. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.19736v1)** (2025). Trains agents through multi-turn interactions with simulated users, studying how reward design and simulator choice improve assistance. **People:** Cheng Qian (Salesforce AI Research; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign), Heng Ji (UIUC), Zuxin Liu and colleagues (Salesforce AI Research).

2. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16523v1)** (2026). Uses a meta-agent to improve user simulators, environments, rewards, and training settings as the agent learns. **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta), Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore), Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology), Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher), Xi Ye (University of Alberta; Amii).

3. **[MIMESIS: Learning User Simulators as Training Environments for Interactive Agents](https://viethoang1512.github.io/mimesis/)** (2026). Learns realistic user simulators from human conversations, then uses simulated interactions and coaching feedback to improve agents. **People:** Hoang Phan (Meta Superintelligence Labs; New York University), Changdae Oh (Meta; University of Wisconsin–Madison), Dat Huynh, Deren Lei, and colleagues at Meta.

4. **[Training Proactive and Personalized LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.02208v1)** (2025). Introduces UserVille’s preference-aware simulated users and reinforcement learning that rewards task success, useful clarification, and personalization. **People:** Weiwei Sun, Xuhui Zhou, Weihua Du, Sean Welleck, Graham Neubig, Maarten Sap, and Yiming Yang; affiliations include Carnegie Mellon University, with Xingyao Wang at OpenHands.
